walkthroughs.body_html:
Quantities & Units in Mechanics — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Quantities & Units in Mechanics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Quantities & Units in Mechanics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A particle starts from rest and accelerates at 4 m/s² for 3 seconds. Final velocity is:
options: 12 m/s
7 m/s

mcqs.q: Which SUVAT equation does NOT involve t?
options: v² = u² + 2as
v = u + at
s = ut + ½at²

mcqs.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. What is the relationship between co-interior (allied) angles?
options: They add up to 180 degrees.
They are equal to each other, like alternate angles.
The magnitude is 12 — you multiply the components.
They add up to 360 degrees because they make a full turn.

mcqs.q: What is the value of x^0 (for x not equal to zero)?
options: x^0 equals 0 because raising something to the zero gives nothing.
1 — any non-zero number to the power of zero equals 1.
x^0 equals x because the zero has no effect.
The magnitude is 12 — you multiply the components.

mcqs.q: What is the magnitude of the vector (3, 4)?
options: The magnitude is 12 — you multiply the components.
They add up to 360 degrees because they make a full turn.
The magnitude is 7 — you add the components.
5 — using sqrt(3^2 + 4^2).
